messages.author: b7aff788b6a63d16
messages.subject: Overlap output
parts:
Dear Chris,

I'm calculating overlap of foraging areas for all my pairs of individuals using the overlap function. I'm getting strange output numbers in the DOF, which are supposed to be between 0 and 1 right?

My data involves 16 bats which are GPS tracked every 2 minutes during 18h-6h every day. Not every bats is tracked the same amount of days, so I am trying to calculate overall foraging areas overlap. First, I calculated the fits then the UDs and later the overlaps for the pairs of individuals (bellow is the code, and in the attachemnt there are the variograms and the the plot of the foraging areas ). Could you tell me why do I get so large numbers in the DOF output of the overlap function?

Thank you so much for your help!
Cheers,
Camila

#calculating fits for all individuals
FITS <- lapply(tele.feb, function(x){
  print(x)
  SVF <- variogram(x) #dt = c(2, 1440 %#% "minutes")))
  GUESS <- ctmm.guess(x,interactive=FALSE, variogram = SVF)
  FITS <- ctmm.select(x,GUESS,trace=2, cores= -1)
  return(FITS)
})

#calculating UDs
UDS <- akde(tele.feb,FITS)

#calculating overlap for pair of  indvs
all_overlap <- vector(mode="list", length= length(UDS))
names(all_overlap) <- names(UDS)

for (i in seq_along(UDS)){
  all_overlap[[i]] <- vector(mode="list", length= length(UDS))
  bat1=UDS[[i]]
  for (j in seq_along(UDS)){
    if (i!=j){
      print(i,j)
      bat2=UDS[[j]]
      comparison=overlap(list(bat1, bat2))
      all_overlap[[i]][[j]]=comparison
     
    }
  }
}

#OUTPUT FOR ONE PAIR
all_overlap[["22507B4E_D"]][[2]]
$DOF
         [,1]     [,2]
[1,]      Inf 158.0873
[2,] 158.0873      Inf

$CI
, , low

          [,1]      [,2]
[1,] 1.0000000 0.2227233
[2,] 0.2227233 1.0000000

, , est

          [,1]      [,2]
[1,] 1.0000000 0.2955741
[2,] 0.2955741 1.0000000

, , high

          [,1]      [,2]
[1,] 1.0000000 0.3809719
[2,] 0.3809719 1.0000000


attr(,"class")
[1] "overlap"

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Overlap output
parts:
Hi Camila,

The DOF values are the "degrees of freedom" or "effective sample size" and should be between 0 and Inf. Larger values >20 indicate good quality data.
The overlap values are in the CI slot and are between 0 and 1, and your overlap estimate (between individuals 1 and 2) here is 0.296 (0.223-0.381).

I will update the documentation, as the addition of the DOF slot was a recent change necessary for some overlap meta-analysis code.
I'll also add code for if the lists aren't named to extract that information from the objects.

Best,
Chris
